observation_summary: The system throws a MockitoException when attempting to call a real method on a spy of an abstract class if that method internally invokes an abstract method. The error message explicitly states that calling real methods is only possible when mocking non-abstract methods.
reasoning_summary: The failure occurs because the system lacks a validation check to distinguish between calling real methods on concrete implementations versus abstract ones. The system attempts to execute a real method that is abstract, leading to an exception. The fix requires adding a guard or condition to verify if the method being invoked is abstract before attempting to call the real implementation, thus preventing the invalid operation.
evidence_used: Cannot call abstract real method on java object!
Calling real methods is only possible when mocking non abstract method.
evidence_gaps: No production code snippet provided to confirm the exact location of the missing check.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The issue is not an incorrect implementation of an algorithm, but rather the failure to validate the state (abstract vs. concrete) before proceeding with the method invocation.
The capability to spy on abstract classes exists, but it lacks the necessary guard to handle abstract method calls safely.
